brief: THE BET — take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. Grep drawSill() (~line 12131) before anything else and confirm the premise for yourself: it is ~90 lines, it draws three objects — two geranium pots and a forgotten cup, from sillPots() — and its ONLY input from the world is `daylight`, via `warm = 0.10 + 0.55 * daylight` and `lit`. Nothing in it reads season(), warmth, growSeason(), snowCover, wetF, raining, windF, chillF or any town state. Yet it is the bottom 7.5% of every frame at every framing (sillTop() = H - max(26, H * 0.075)), it is drawn at sillU() scale so its objects are the largest figures in the picture, and it is the one place in the world the observer is nominally standing. Make the ledge a place the year and the weather pass through: geraniums that come on and die back, rain that beads on the glass and darkens the stone, a rim of snow or frost on the outer nosing in winter, the cup that comes and goes. What exactly it holds is yours to choose — the requirement is that a February evening and a July morning are two different pictures at the bottom of the frame, and that the difference is legible at the shipping size. The sill domain has had ZERO new elements in 190 iterations; this is the piece's framing device and it has never changed.
successLooksLike: Two shots at one seed, size and hour — one in February, one in July — and the bottom of the frame is two different pictures, quoted as diff MASS against a same-code control that reads 0. Plus: the ground cache's repaint rate is still at or under #180's 75.14/day (probes/ground-rebuilds.mjs exists), and whatever you put on the ledge ANSWERS THE POINTER — c282, folded in here: the pots and the cup have never had a name.
avoid: drawSill is baked INTO the ground cache, from inside drawOurSide. Anything that must be true per frame is a live overlay drawn after, not a new reason to rebuild the cache — #180 cut the repaint rate 110.78 -> 75.14/day and this must not push it back; measure it, do not assume it. Nothing here may draw from R(): the sill is a CANVAS-EXTENT population and the draws a frame spends are a fact about the WINDOW, so use hash(). And do NOT crowd it — the sill is the frame, and the change through the year is the content, not the number of objects. If you end with more silhouettes than you started with and they do not each earn their place, you have made a shelf, not a sill.
